questions.q: What five DMV queries from earlier lessons does this view pull together?
options: Sessions, slow queries, missing indexes, blocking, and fragmentation
Backup, restore, differential, log, and point-in-time recovery
Five unrelated queries never covered earlier in this chapter
Only the missing-index query from Lesson 6, repeated five times
questions.explain: The chapter used these five DMV-based queries at five different points; the dashboard view consolidates the three highest-value ones.

questions.q: What does UNION ALL accomplish in dbo.vw_HealthDashboard?
options: Combines the blocking, slow-query, and fragmentation result sets into one scannable result
Deletes duplicate rows automatically, unlike UNION
Joins two tables on a shared key column
Filters out any row with a NULL value
questions.explain: UNION ALL stacks the three separate signal queries into one combined result set, each tagged with a 'signal' label.

questions.q: What does the 'signal' column make easier?
options: Immediately identifying which category (blocking, slow query, fragmentation) a given row belongs to
Automatically fixing the underlying problem without any further action
Sorting rows alphabetically by table name only
Connecting to a different Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: The signal column labels each row's category, avoiding the need to re-derive that from raw DMV columns every time.

questions.q: What is the real difference between reactive and proactive monitoring, as this lesson describes it?
options: Reactive investigates only after a complaint arrives; proactive catches the same signals on a regular schedule before that
Reactive and proactive monitoring use completely different DMVs with no overlap
Proactive monitoring requires deleting all existing indexes first
There is no real difference — both terms mean the same thing
questions.explain: Every fix earlier in this chapter started from a complaint; a dashboard checked regularly can catch the same signals earlier.

questions.q: What does querying this one view replace?
options: Manually running five separate queries in the right order every time someone complains
The need to ever read an execution plan again
The CREATE INDEX statement from Lesson 7
The Elastic Jobs schedule from Lesson 11
questions.explain: Instead of remembering and running five separate DMV queries by hand, one view surfaces all three highest-value signals together.
